chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Isma'il ibn Sa'd al-Ash'ari, who said:

I asked al-Rida (peace be upon him) about the man who touches the private part of his young girl until she discharges water, without him having sexual intercourse, playing with her with his hand until she discharges. He (peace be upon him) said: 'When she discharges due to desire/excitement, then the ritual bath (ghusl) is upon her.'
ai.seo_question: Does a woman need to perform ghusl if she is masturbated by her husband?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies that the obligation of ghusl is determined by the physiological discharge of sexual fluid (madhiy or mani) resulting from desire, rather than the specific act of intercourse itself. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that ritual purity depends on the emission of fluid due to sexual gratification, distinguishing it from mere physical contact without emission. It serves as a foundational text for understanding the mechanics of major ritual impurity (janabah) in personal hygiene and worship.
